summary: Describe bounded polynomial kernels from Ore monic division uniformly, including generator degrees needed for all graded thresholds.
Prove non-invariance of boundary-divisor components under Möbius flow to obtain the all-m weight-two codimension step.
Extend the configuration-to-Grassmannian map to scaled compactifications for uniform fibre bounds, accounting for boundary-approach rates.
Use a closed EPD Riemann function to express all-order cross-block Goursat lifts and the kernel's order filtration uniformly.
Test effective-Hamiltonian block elimination for higher-order kernel lifts and a coupling-channel rank bound beyond order two.
Prove transversality of the explicit large-cluster space to coordinate flags to justify expected Richardson contact codimension.
Use restricted divisors and local intersection multiplicities to detect repeated discriminant components, resolving bad-factor exponents.
Analyze genuine trinomial normal forms at merging neck rings and their discriminant exponents, testing when the model or simple vanishing fails.
Use matched face, neck and bubble counts to detect missing degeneration layers, including possible new layers at merging loci.
Control local monodromy at remainder branch components to test reducedness beyond the good-trace transpositions.
Find an independent Euler characteristic for the general-line Weierstrass cover and use Riemann–Hurwitz to test discriminant reducedness.
Prove the two-minimizer condition uniformly through local valuated-matroid exchanges, potentially using one-column Laplace expansion.
Factor leading window minors shell by shell to prove valuations for all cluster and block sizes.
Derive coefficient p-adic valuations for neck polynomials and test Newton-polygon irreducibility as a route to squarefreeness.
Relate neck-window valuation jumps to coefficient-stream linear complexity and Hankel rank beyond the tested rank-two case.
Prove the balanced multi-species filling formula for neck leading levels and the determinant product giving their leading coefficients.
Identify joint orthogonality structure for nested-support ratio functions to prove mixed Hankel nonvanishing; standard Nikishin hypotheses fail.
Run block Lanczos recursion for cluster ratio channels and test nonbreakdown and block sizes as joint Hankel cost bounds.
Derive general-cluster moment entry orders, solve their assignment problem and prove nonvanishing of the tight determinant.
Use affineness of M0,N to formulate and prove a boundary-incidence dimension criterion excluding divisorial weight-three loci.
Test versality of local Wronskian unfoldings at triple zeros to obtain boundary weight-three codimension bounds.
Test whether only symmetry forces divisorial weight-three coincidences, using the codimension of symmetric branch configurations.
Develop recursive single merges and explicit neck polynomials to reduce discriminant reducedness to the final cross-ratio family.
Prove neck pencils are Lefschetz across cluster types, with simple double roots at distinct parameters away from special points.
Develop boundary factorization recursion for reducedness, proving merge closure and lower-point factor identities beyond one paired side.
Replace rigid simplicity by absence of triple far roots where the weight-three criterion suffices; retain the unresolved two-wall neck obstruction.
Organize far-point degree drops by counting states escaping to branch points at the half-exponent threshold; counts alone do not prove simplicity.
Reduce corner initial minors to Birkhoff interpolation and test Pólya failure for nonvertices, extending Laplace splits beyond (2,n).
Test Jacobi-polynomial bases for far spaces and possible Young-diagram Wronskian methods, starting with X(2,3).
Apply orthogonal-polynomial determinant sign bounds to zero-free regions of the classical half, keeping its Wronskian separate from Rn,k.
Interpret classical-half Wronskians as Darboux–Crum transforms and test pairing regularity; root simplicity requires a separate argument.
Test total-positive integral kernels for zero-free Wronskians, preserving the known failure of the P3 Chebyshev-system proposal.
Use confluent Hermite-jet initial determinants to prove block-three/four neck vanishing orders and power-sum Hankel leading factors.
Seek a uniform transitive Galois or monodromy argument for far polynomials as a route to squarefreeness.
Prove local asymptotic zero separation for last-step far polynomials and reduce triple-root exclusion to a finite residual range.
Find a universal local limit with simple zeros for merging far-root chains, then justify large-parameter exclusion by Hurwitz.
Use exact six-space gcd checks to cover the finite range below a proved asymptotic threshold for last-step far polynomials.
Test an avoided-crossing mechanism for approaching far-root chains, distinguishing continued approach from actual saturation or merging.
Apply varying-parameter Jacobi asymptotics and Rodrigues to obtain nonvanishing amplitudes in the far polynomial's two-term expansion.
Derive a phase-quantization rule for far-root chains that proves simple separated roots, beyond observed odd-integer offsets.
Estimate six-space coefficient magnitudes and use Ostrowski's polygon to prove the four-circle root-modulus law.
Express the four-circle law through four long tropical coefficient-hull pieces and prove their asymptotic structure.
Use reduced-space exact gcd checks for the finite middle-step range, accounting for the recorded expensive l=3 case.
Test and prove 4l long Newton-hull edges for middle-step far polynomials to extend the circle asymptotic route uniformly in k.
Relate middle-step tropical hull pieces to root circles beyond the tested l=2 eight-piece pattern.
